title: Praise Allah, greet His chosen, then ask the question.
subtitle: How the second half of the surah opens
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to {idea}praise Allah for His innumerable blessings{/idea} and send peace on His chosen servants. Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd said these are the Prophets; Ath-Thawri and As-Suddi said the Companions, and Ibn Kathir says both fit. Then comes the question: {trap}is Allah better, or what they set up beside Him?{/trap}
now: Before you argue with anyone about faith, start like this: thank Allah, pray for the good people who came before you. {idea}Then ask yourself the question first.{/idea} What do you actually lean on when things get hard?
old: Talking about Allah starts with proving people wrong.
new: It starts with praise and peace, and then an honest question about what I rely on.
try: Before your next prayer, say al-hamdu lillah and send peace on the Prophet ﷺ.

title: You plant the seed. Can you make the tree grow?
subtitle: Gardens of beauty from rain
then: Ibn Kathir says the idolators of Makkah {idea}admitted Allah created everything and sends the rain{/idea}, yet worshipped others who they admitted could create nothing. The verse asks: is there a god with Allah? The answer: {trap}they set up equals to Him.{/trap}
now: You water the tomato plant on your balcony every evening. One morning there is fruit. {idea}You did your part, but you did not make it grow.{/idea} Same with your career, your kids, your savings.
old: What I worked for, I produced.
new: I plant and water, and Allah is the one who makes anything grow.
try: Look at one plant or tree today and say subhanAllah for what you did not make.

title: Stable ground under your feet is a gift.
subtitle: Earth, rivers, mountains, and a barrier
then: Ibn Kathir explains the earth is made {reward}smooth and calm by His grace{/reward}, since a shaking earth would be no place to live. Rivers flow where people need them, and a barrier keeps sweet and salt water apart so each stays as it is meant to be. Yet {trap}most of them do not know.{/trap}
now: You fall asleep in an apartment building. You fill a glass from the tap. You never think the floor might move. {idea}Every quiet, ordinary day is resting on something He arranged.{/idea}
old: Solid ground and clean water are just how the world is.
new: The ground that holds still and the water I drink are daily mercies from Allah.
try: Drink your next glass of water slowly and thank Allah for it before you swallow.

title: Who answers you when you are desperate?
subtitle: The One the distressed call on
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is {idea}the One people call on in difficulty and turn to when calamity strikes.{/idea} He cites the Prophet ﷺ telling a man he called people to Allah, who relieves harm and returns the lost. The verse ends: {trap}little do you remember.{/trap}
now: The hospital corridor at 3am. The phone call you cannot believe. You pray like never before. {idea}He answers the desperate.{/idea} The test is whether you still remember Him a month later, when it is all fine.
old: I will pray hard when something serious happens.
new: The One who answered me in my worst moment deserves my remembrance on ordinary days too.
try: Remember one hard time Allah got you through. Thank Him for it today.

title: Guided through darkness, rain announced by wind.
subtitle: Signposts and good news in nature
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah guides people {idea}by the heavenly and earthly signposts He created{/idea}, like the stars. He sends winds ahead of the rain clouds, {reward}His mercy to servants suffering drought and despair.{/reward}
now: Driving home late on a dark road, the map app finds your way. The cool wind before a storm after a heatwave. {idea}Every way through darkness was set up by Him.{/idea}
old: Finding my way is just technology and skill.
new: Every light that guides me through the dark, and every hint of relief, comes from Allah.
try: The next time you feel a breeze, say al-hamdu lillah for His mercy.

title: He started creation and will do it again.
subtitle: Show your proof, if you have any
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}originates creation by His might and then repeats it.{/idea} Rain goes into the earth, comes out as springs, and brings crops and flowers. The listeners are told to produce proof for other gods, but {trap}they have no proof or evidence.{/trap}
now: You look at an ultrasound, a tiny heartbeat on a screen. {idea}The One who did this once can do it again.{/idea} If He began you, bringing you back is not hard for Him.
old: Coming back to life after death is hard to imagine.
new: The One who created me the first time can easily do it again.
try: Look at a photo of yourself as a baby and reflect on who made you.

title: Only Allah knows the unseen.
subtitle: No one knows when the Hour comes

key.label: Who to ask about the future

then: Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}an absolute exception{/idea}: no one besides Allah knows the unseen. He cites the hadith where the Prophet ﷺ told Jibril about the Hour: {idea}the one being asked does not know more than the one asking.{/idea}
now: The horoscope app. The friend who "just knows" how things will turn out. Your own anxious mind running every scenario. {idea}None of them hold the keys.{/idea} You can let go of needing to know.
old: If I could just know what is coming, I would feel safe.
new: Only Allah knows what is coming, so I can rest in trusting Him.
try: When you catch yourself worrying about the future today, say "Allah knows" and breathe.

title: Their knowledge stopped short, then doubt, then blindness.
subtitle: Three steps away from the Hereafter
then: Ibn Kathir explains their {trap}knowledge and amazement stopped short of knowing its time{/trap}, and that the disbelievers {trap}doubt it will come to pass{/trap}. Finally they are {trap}blind and completely ignorant about it.{/trap}
now: You know a lot about your industry, your favorite team, the latest phones. Ask about the Hereafter and it gets vague. {trap}Not thinking about it turns into doubting it.{/trap} Doubt left alone becomes not seeing at all.
old: I will think about the afterlife properly when I am older.
new: Leaving the Hereafter unexamined slowly turns into doubt and then blindness.
try: Spend five minutes today reading or listening to something about the Hereafter.

title: Dust and bones, they asked, brought back?
subtitle: The doubt about resurrection
then: Ibn Kathir says the idolators denied the Resurrection, {trap}considering it extremely unlikely that bodies will be re-created after they have become bones and dust.{/trap} The verse before had just said He begins creation and repeats it.
now: You stand at a grave on a cold morning, the earth freshly turned over someone you loved. It feels final. {idea}The verse answers that feeling.{/idea} Dust is not the end of the story for the One who made you from it.
old: Once someone is buried, that is the end.
new: Dust is not too far gone for the One who created from nothing.
try: Make dua today for someone you have lost, by name.

title: We have heard this forever, they said. Old stories.
subtitle: When familiarity breeds dismissal
then: Ibn Kathir explains their words: {trap}we and our forefathers have been hearing this for a long time, but we have never seen it happen.{/trap} They called it tales passed down from old books, with no basis in reality.
now: You have heard about death and judgment since you were a kid in Quran class. {trap}It has become background noise.{/trap} Hearing something often does not make it less true.
old: I have heard this all my life, so it feels like old stories.
new: A truth I have heard many times is still true, and still coming.
try: Read one verse about the Hereafter today as if hearing it for the first time.

title: Go and look at how it ended for them.
subtitle: History as evidence
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was told to answer them this way: look at {trap}how the punishment struck those who denied the Messengers{/trap} and how {reward}Allah saved the Messengers and the believers who followed them.{/reward} That itself shows the Message is true.
now: You visit old ruins on holiday, or read about a family empire that collapsed. {idea}Do not just take the photo.{/idea} Ask what they relied on, and how it ended.
old: History is a list of old facts.
new: The endings of past people are evidence I am meant to look at and learn from.
try: On your next trip or history read, find one lesson about how something ended.

title: Do not grieve over them or be crushed by plots.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ
then: Ibn Kathir explains this was {idea}to comfort the Prophet ﷺ{/idea}: do not feel sorry for them or {trap}kill yourself with regret{/trap}, and do not be distressed by their plotting, because {reward}Allah will help and support you.{/reward}
now: Your brother will not listen. Your friend keeps making the same bad choice. You lie awake replaying it. {idea}Care, advise, pray, and then let Allah carry what you cannot.{/idea}
old: If someone I love rejects good advice, it is my failure.
new: I can grieve for people without being crushed, because their choices and my support belong to Allah.
try: Make dua for one person you are worried about, then consciously hand it to Allah.

title: So when is it coming, they mocked.
subtitle: Asking for a date to avoid the question
then: Ibn Kathir says the idolators asked about the Day of Resurrection {trap}but thought it unlikely that it would ever come to pass.{/trap} The question was not curiosity. It was a challenge: if it is real, give us a date.
now: "Everyone has been saying the end is near for centuries." You hear it at the dinner table, or you think it yourself. {idea}The date is not yours to know.{/idea} Your readiness is.
old: Without a date, I do not need to think about it seriously.
new: Not knowing when is the very reason to be ready now.
try: Ask yourself honestly: if it were tomorrow, what one thing would I fix today? Fix it.

title: What you rush toward may already be behind you.
subtitle: Closer than you think
then: Ibn Abbas said: {trap}that which you wish to hasten on has come close to you, or some of it has.{/trap} Mujahid, Qatadah and As-Suddi held the same view. The Prophet ﷺ was told to answer the mocking question with this.
now: You keep saying you will sort your prayers out after the wedding, after the move, after the kids grow. {trap}The end is not waiting for your schedule.{/trap} It might be one step behind you.
old: I have plenty of time to get ready.
new: What I keep postponing may be much closer than I think.
try: Do one thing today that you have been saving for "later" in your faith.
